title: Beyond Trade-offs: A Unified Framework for Privacy, Robustness, and Communication Efficiency in Federated Learning

C-a.quote: clients compute gradients based on the current global model, perturb them with DP noise, and apply a momentum-based update to strengthen robustness against malicious attacks [49]
C-a.locator: Sec. 1; C-a reaches two on the CLIENT MOMENTUM and the ROBUST AVERAGING, each defense-purposed on the paper's own words. Momentum is the quotation above; the aggregation rule is "To ensure Byzantine robustness, we employ an aggregation rule AGG that satisfies (b, κ)-Robust Averaging [9]" (Sec. 4). AMENDMENT 3 EXCLUDES THE OTHER TWO COMPONENTS AND THIS IS THE PAPER WHERE THAT MATTERS MOST, since they are the paper's headline contributions: the Gaussian mechanism is privacy-purposed ("employs Gaussian noise as a DP mechanism", Sec. 1) and the JL compression is communication-purposed ("compression method C OMPRESS to reduce the uplink communication", Sec. 4, and "The bidirectional communication cost, i.e., from each client to the federator and from the federator to each client, is reduced from O(d) to O(k) per round", Sec. 5). Amendment 3 RAISES this row's code, because momentum reads by name as an optimizer device and the paper states a robustness purpose for it

C-b.quote: the robustness guarantee that a robust aggregation holds in the original vector space is preserved in the compressed vector space resulting from the JL transform
C-b.locator: Sec. 1; the paper's reason for composing is GUARANTEE PRESERVATION, not constituent complementarity -- it proves that adding the compression does not destroy what the aggregator already provides, "We theoretically prove that the JL transform satisfies the robust-compatible property under the robust averaging criterion given in [9]" (Sec. 1). That is a non-interference argument and C-b's frozen text admits only standalone effectiveness or complementary threat coverage. For the two components that DO count toward C-a, momentum and robust averaging, no reason for pairing is given at all: momentum arrives with a citation and a single clause, and nothing states what it covers that the aggregator does not. Rule 3 also selects this reading

C-c.quote: Fig. 3 shows the test accuracy of R O B AJ O L on non-i.i.d. CIFAR-10 under various attacks, compared to the baseline, with σNM = 0.1 and kd = 10.
C-c.locator: Sec. 6, Fig. 3 and Tables I-IV; the assembled scheme's own test accuracy under attack is the evidence, over CIFAR-10, Fashion MNIST and FEMNIST, against six attacks (LF, ALIE, SF, Min-Max, Min-Sum and FoE) and three robust aggregation rules, with means and standard deviations over three seeds and a no-attack baseline on every table ("Baseline for noise multiplier = 0.2 is 59.6 ± 0.3%"). The composed claim is read off those numbers: "The experimental results in Fig. 3 indicate that, given robust aggregation rules satisfying the robust averaging criterion, the use of the JL transform as the compression method preserves robustness against malicious attacks"

C-d.quote: We also report the test accuracy on FEMNIST under FoE attack and with Krum as the robust aggregation rule without DP and compression (σNM = 0 and kd = 1).
C-d.locator: Sec. 6, Table IV footnote, plus Tables I-III and Fig. 5; THIS IS THE FRAME'S MOST SYSTEMATIC C-d AND IT RUNS IN TWO INDEPENDENT UPSTREAM DIMENSIONS. The quoted arm switches BOTH upstream stages off at once (σNM = 0, kd = 1) with Krum, the attack and the dataset held fixed, and the outcome is reported against the composed arm. The graded versions are the compression rate over {10, 30, 50} -- "Fig. 4 shows the test accuracy of R O B AJ O L on non-i.i.d. CIFAR-10, at increasing compression rate, and noise multiplier σNM = 0.1" -- and the noise multiplier over {0.1, 0.2, ...} with the rule fixed, "TABLE III: We set noise multiplier σNM = 0.2. We report the test accuracy (unit: %) on non-i.i.d. CIFAR-10 under various attacks and use Trimmed Mean (TM) as the robust aggregation", each sweep repeated for the other rules and all six attacks. The theory is about the same object: the robust-compatibility result states when the downstream guarantee survives the upstream transformation, an ANALYTIC route to the same contrast, so this row could equally be stratified as analytic

C-e.quote: Our theoretical analysis establishes the compatibility of JL transform with robust averaging, ensuring that R O B AJ O L maintains robustness guarantees, satisfies DP, and substantially reduces communication overhead.
C-e.locator: Abstract; the claim states what one constituent does to another's contribution within the composition, which is the attribution C-e asks for, and it is proved rather than measured. The momentum quotation in C-a's locator is a second constituent-level attribution, and the empirical version is the accuracy degradation reported against each noise multiplier and compression rate. The empirical constituent-level attribution is separate and graded: "It suggests that a higher compression rate introduces greater distortion, and therefore, while improving communication efficiency, can lead to performance loss" (Sec. 6), and for the other upstream stage, "as the noise multiplier increases, utility decreases while stronger privacy guarantees are" obtained (Sec. 6)

coder_note:
THIS PAPER PROVES A COMPOSITION-INVARIANCE RESULT, AND THAT MAKES IT THE MOST RELEVANT RELATED WORK THE AUDIT HAS TURNED UP FOR THE PAPER'S OWN ARGUMENT. Its central theorem is that a robust aggregation rule's guarantee, stated in the original vector space, is preserved when an upstream JL compression is inserted -- i.e. it identifies a condition under which composing an upstream transformation with a fixed downstream mechanism does not change what the downstream mechanism delivers. That is the same question our Prop. prop:identification_full and the composition-invariance discussion ask, arrived at from the communication-efficiency literature and answered analytically for one specific pair. A3 and A5 should cite it: it is external evidence that the composition question is live and non-trivial, and it is a case where the answer is POSITIVE, which our own attenuation results say is regime-dependent. It also means the frame contains at least one paper that does the identification properly and knows why it matters.

C-b = NO IS THE DECIDING CODE AND IT INTRODUCES A SIXTH KIND OF PAIRING REASON THAT C-b DOES NOT ADMIT: GUARANTEE PRESERVATION. The attested kinds are now cost complementarity (BRFL), matched threat complementarity (LASA, DDFed, FLTG, SafeSparse), adversarial complementarity (WFAgg), residual coverage (RKD, DROP, DP2Guard, CLIP-Fed), mathematical convenience (FedSAC, not admitted) and non-interference (this paper, not admitted). A5 must report all six with which ones C-b's frozen text admits, because two of the six are grounds for a NO and a reader needs to see that the criterion is narrower than the phrase "reason for pairing" suggests. I did not widen it: the text was frozen before coding and it says what it says.

AMENDMENT 3 RAISES THE CODE FOR THE FOURTH TIME, AND HERE IT INVERTS THE PAPER'S OWN EMPHASIS. Fedward, LASA and RKD were the earlier three. In this paper the two components a name-based reading would count -- DP noise and JL compression, the framework's headline contributions -- are both EXCLUDED on stated purpose, while the component that carries the code is client momentum, which the paper mentions in one clause with a citation. So the amendment does not merely trim the count; it can relocate a paper's C-a onto a component the paper itself treats as incidental. That is an honest consequence of reading purpose off the paper rather than off the operation's name, and A5 should state it as such.

ROUTE STRATIFICATION NOTE: I recorded hyperparameter-sweep because the empirical contrast is what a reader can check, but this row has a legitimate claim to the analytic route as well, and it is the only row in the frame where both are strong. If A5 reports route counts, this paper should be flagged rather than silently assigned, since a single-route tally understates how the identification is actually established here.
